```{r}
# ============================================================================
# METHOD 1: PRE-WHITENING APPROACH (Yue et al., 2002)
# ============================================================================
# Removes autocorrelation, tests residuals, then restores trend magnitude

cat("\n", rep("=", 70), "\n")
cat("METHOD 1: PRE-WHITENED MANN-KENDALL TEST\n")
cat(rep("=", 70), "\n\n")

library(trend)

# Step 1: Estimate AR(1) coefficient
rho1 <- acf(storminess_ts_weighted, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]
cat(sprintf("Step 1: AR(1) coefficient (ρ₁) = %.4f\n", rho1))

# Step 2: Remove autocorrelation (pre-whiten)
# Y_t' = Y_t - ρ₁ * Y_{t-1}
n <- length(storminess_ts_weighted)
prewhitened <- storminess_ts_weighted[2:n] - rho1 * storminess_ts_weighted[1:(n-1)]

cat(sprintf("Step 2: Pre-whitened series created (n = %d)\n", length(prewhitened)))

# Verify autocorrelation removed
rho1_pw <- acf(prewhitened, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]
cat(sprintf("         Residual ρ₁ = %.4f (should be ≈ 0)\n", rho1_pw))

# Step 3: Apply standard Mann-Kendall to pre-whitened series
mk_pw <- mk.test(prewhitened)

cat(sprintf("\nStep 3: Mann-Kendall on Pre-whitened Data:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Test statistic: %.4f\n", mk_pw$statistic))
cat(sprintf("  p-value: %.4f\n", mk_pw$p.value))

# Step 4: Calculate trend using Sen's slope on ORIGINAL data
# (Pre-whitening is ONLY for significance testing, not magnitude estimation)
sens_original <- sens.slope(storminess_ts_weighted)

cat(sprintf("\nStep 4: Trend Magnitude (from original data):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Sen's slope: %.4f m⁴/s⁴/month\n", sens_original$estimates))
cat(sprintf("  Annual: %.4f m⁴/s⁴/year\n", sens_original$estimates * 12))
cat(sprintf("  67-year change: %.2f m⁴/s⁴\n", sens_original$estimates * 804))

# Final conclusion
if (mk_pw$p.value < 0.05) {
  cat(sprintf("\n SIGNIFICANT TREND (p = %.4f)\n", mk_pw$p.value))
  cat(sprintf("  Direction: %s\n", ifelse(mk_pw$statistic > 0, "INCREASING", "DECREASING")))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("\nNo significant trend detected (p = %.4f)\n", mk_pw$p.value))
  cat("Despite autocorrelation correction, trend is not statistically significant.\n")
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# METHOD 2: GENERALIZED LEAST SQUARES WITH AR(1) ERRORS
# ============================================================================

library(nlme)

cat("\n", rep("=", 70), "\n")
cat("METHOD 2: GLS REGRESSION WITH AR(1) ERRORS\n")
cat(rep("=", 70), "\n\n")

# Create time index
time_index <- 1:length(storminess_ts_weighted)
data_df <- data.frame(
  storminess = storminess_ts_weighted,
  time = time_index
)

# Fit GLS with AR(1) correlation structure
gls_model <- gls(storminess ~ time, 
                 data = data_df,
                 correlation = corAR1(form = ~ time),
                 method = "ML")

# Extract results
gls_summary <- summary(gls_model)
slope <- coef(gls_model)[2]
slope_pval <- gls_summary$tTable[2, 4]

cat("GLS Model Results:\n")
print(gls_summary$tTable)

cat(sprintf("\nTrend Estimates:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Slope: %.4f m⁴/s⁴/month\n", slope))
cat(sprintf("  Annual: %.4f m⁴/s⁴/year\n", slope * 12))
cat(sprintf("  p-value: %.4f\n", slope_pval))
cat(sprintf("  Estimated ρ: %.4f\n", 
            coef(gls_model$modelStruct$corStruct, unconstrained = FALSE)))

if (slope_pval < 0.05) {
  cat(sprintf("\n SIGNIFICANT TREND (p = %.4f)\n", slope_pval))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("\nNo significant trend (p = %.4f)\n", slope_pval))
}

cat("\n GLS explicitly models AR(1) structure - most rigorous approach.\n")
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# METHOD 3: BLOCK BOOTSTRAP CONFIDENCE INTERVALS
# ============================================================================

library(boot)

cat("\n", rep("=", 70), "\n")
cat("METHOD 3: BLOCK BOOTSTRAP APPROACH\n")
cat(rep("=", 70), "\n\n")

# Function to calculate slope
slope_stat <- function(data, indices) {
  sens.slope(data[indices])$estimates
}

# Block length based on autocorrelation
# Rule of thumb: block_length ≈ 1/(1-ρ₁)
block_length <- ceiling(1 / (1 - rho1))
cat(sprintf("Block length: %d months (based on ρ₁ = %.3f)\n", block_length, rho1))

# Block bootstrap with 10,000 replicates
set.seed(42)
boot_result <- tsboot(storminess_ts_weighted, 
                      slope_stat, 
                      R = 10000, 
                      l = block_length,
                      sim = "fixed")

# Calculate confidence interval
boot_ci <- boot.ci(boot_result, type = "perc")

cat(sprintf("\nBootstrap Results (10,000 replicates):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Observed slope: %.4f m⁴/s⁴/month\n", boot_result$t0))
cat(sprintf("  Bootstrap SE: %.4f\n", sd(boot_result$t)))
cat(sprintf("  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", 
            boot_ci$percent[4], boot_ci$percent[5]))

# Test if CI includes zero
ci_includes_zero <- boot_ci$percent[4] < 0 & boot_ci$percent[5] > 0

if (!ci_includes_zero) {
  cat("\n✓ Confidence interval does NOT include zero - significant trend\n")
} else {
  cat("\nConfidence interval includes zero - no significant trend\n")
}

cat("\n Block bootstrap preserves autocorrelation structure.\n")
```

## 2.2 Regional Sub-Analysis: Svalbard Trend

[cite_start]To investigate trends in a key hotspot of coastal change, a sub-analysis was performed for the Svalbard region[cite: 4, 47, 6202].

### 2.2.1 Domain Subsetting and Time Series Generation

A regional domain was defined by a geographical bounding box (74°N to 81°N, 10°E to 35°E). The storminess data array was subsetted to this domain, creating a new regional dataset. [cite_start]Critically, a new area-weighted time series was then generated specifically for this smaller domain to create a physically representative index for the Svalbard region[cite: 6203, 6204].

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# PHASE 2 - SUB-ANALYSIS: SVALBARD REGIONAL TREND
# ============================================================================

# --- 1. Define the Svalbard Bounding Box ---
# These are approximate coordinates for the Svalbard region.
# Longitude is from 10°E to 35°E.
# Latitude is from 74°N to 81°N.
lon_svalbard <- which(lon >= 10 & lon <= 35)
lat_svalbard <- which(lat >= 74 & lat <= 81)

cat("--- Subsetting data for the Svalbard region ---\n")
cat(sprintf("Longitude indices: %d to %d\n", min(lon_svalbard), max(lon_svalbard)))
cat(sprintf("Latitude indices: %d to %d\n", min(lat_svalbard), max(lat_svalbard)))

# --- 2. Extract the Svalbard-only data ---
# Remember, the full array is [time, lat, lon]
storminess_svalbard <- storminess[, lat_svalbard, lon_svalbard]
lat_svalbard_vals <- lat[lat_svalbard]
lon_svalbard_vals <- lon[lon_svalbard]

cat(sprintf("Dimensions of Svalbard data: [time, lat, lon] = [%d, %d, %d]\n",
            dim(storminess_svalbard)[1],
            dim(storminess_svalbard)[2],
            dim(storminess_svalbard)[3]))
```

```{r}
# --- Verification Step 1: Numerically Check the Coordinate Ranges ---

# Get the actual lat/lon values from your original coordinate vectors
selected_lats <- lat[lat_svalbard]
selected_lons <- lon[lon_svalbard]

cat("\n--- NUMERICAL VERIFICATION ---\n")
cat("Desired Latitude Range: 74°N to 81°N\n")
cat(sprintf("Selected Latitude Range: %.2f to %.2f\n", min(selected_lats), max(selected_lats)))

cat("\nDesired Longitude Range: 10°E to 35°E\n")
cat(sprintf("Selected Longitude Range: %.2f to %.2f\n", min(selected_lons), max(selected_lons)))

if (min(selected_lats) >= 74 & max(selected_lats) <= 81) {
    cat(" Latitude selection is correct.\n")
} else {
    cat(" WARNING: Latitude selection is incorrect.\n")
}
```

```{r}
# --- 3. Create a NEW Area-Weighted Time Series for Svalbard ---
# This is a critical step. We must re-calculate the average for the new domain.
weights_svalbard <- cos(lat_svalbard_vals * pi / 180)
weights_matrix_svalbard <- matrix(weights_svalbard,
                                  nrow = length(lat_svalbard_vals),
                                  ncol = length(lon_svalbard_vals),
                                  byrow = FALSE)

storm_ts_svalbard <- apply(storminess_svalbard, 1, function(slice) {
  weighted.mean(slice, weights_matrix_svalbard, na.rm = TRUE)
})

cat("\n Area-weighted time series for Svalbard created. Length:", length(storm_ts_svalbard), "\n")
```

```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Prepare data frame with true ERA5 month-end timestamps
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
storm_df_svalbard <- data.frame(
  date = as.Date(time_dates),        # from decoded vector (month-end)
  storminess = storm_ts_svalbard
)
```

### 2.2.2 Regional Trend Analysis

The full trend analysis pipeline was re-applied to the new Svalbard time series. The regional data exhibited a lag-1 autocorrelation of $\rho_1 = 0.436$, confirming the need for autocorrelation-corrected methods.

* **Trend Significance:** For this analysis, the **pre-whitened Mann-Kendall test** was used. This standard climatological method removes the autoregressive lag-1 component from the time series before applying the standard Mann-Kendall test to the resulting residuals. The test returned a p-value of **0.9933**, indicating a complete absence of a statistically significant trend.

* **Trend Magnitude:** The Theil-Sen slope estimator calculated a trend of **0.0072 m⁴/s⁴ per month**, corresponding to a total change of 3.4% over the baseline period. The 95% confidence interval for this slope was **[-0.0231, 0.0374]**. As with the Pan-Arctic analysis, this interval contains zero, independently confirming the non-significant result from the pre-whitened Mann-Kendall test.

The conclusion for the Svalbard region is identical to that for the Pan-Arctic as a whole: there is no statistically significant trend in storminess from 1958–2024.

![Svalbard Regional Storminess Index (1958–2024)](image_762ee7.png)

```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Check autocorrelation (ρ₁)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
rho1_svalbard <- acf(storm_ts_svalbard, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]
cat(sprintf("\nLag-1 Autocorrelation (ρ₁): %.3f\n", rho1_svalbard))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Pre-whitened Mann-Kendall test for significance
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n--- Pre-whitened Mann-Kendall Test (Svalbard) ---\n")
n_svalbard <- length(storm_ts_svalbard)
prewhitened_svalbard <- storm_ts_svalbard[2:n_svalbard] - rho1_svalbard * storm_ts_svalbard[1:(n_svalbard-1)]
mk_pw_svalbard <- mk.test(prewhitened_svalbard)

cat(sprintf("  Test statistic: %.4f\n", mk_pw_svalbard$statistic))
cat(sprintf("  p-value: %.4f\n", mk_pw_svalbard$p.value))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Sen’s Slope Estimation (Robust Trend Magnitude)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n--- Sen's Slope Estimator (Svalbard) ---\n")
sens_svalbard <- sens.slope(storm_ts_svalbard)
slope_monthly_svalbard <- sens_svalbard$estimates
ci_lower <- sens_svalbard$conf.int[1]
ci_upper <- sens_svalbard$conf.int[2]

# Derived values
slope_decade_svalbard <- slope_monthly_svalbard * 12 * 10
total_change_svalbard <- slope_monthly_svalbard * length(storm_ts_svalbard)
baseline_mean_svalbard <- mean(storm_ts_svalbard[1:120])
pct_change_svalbard <- (total_change_svalbard / baseline_mean_svalbard) * 100

cat(sprintf("  Slope: %.4f m⁴/s⁴ per month\n", slope_monthly_svalbard))
cat(sprintf("  95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", ci_lower, ci_upper))
cat(sprintf("  10-year trend: %.4f m⁴/s⁴ per decade\n", slope_decade_svalbard))
cat(sprintf("  Total change (1958–2024): %.2f m⁴/s⁴ (%.1f%%)\n",
            total_change_svalbard, pct_change_svalbard))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Build trend line for visualization
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
intercept_svalbard <- storm_df_svalbard$storminess[1]
trend_line_svalbard <- intercept_svalbard + slope_monthly_svalbard * (1:nrow(storm_df_svalbard))
storm_df_svalbard$trend <- trend_line_svalbard

# Confidence interval lines
storm_df_svalbard$trend_upper <- intercept_svalbard + ci_upper * (1:nrow(storm_df_svalbard))
storm_df_svalbard$trend_lower <- intercept_svalbard + ci_lower * (1:nrow(storm_df_svalbard))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Plot Svalbard Trend (with 95% CI)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot(storm_df_svalbard, aes(x = date, y = storminess)) +
  geom_line(color = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = trend_lower, ymax = trend_upper),
              fill = "#D55E00", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(aes(y = trend), color = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1.1) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +z
  labs(
    title = "Svalbard Regional Storminess Index (1958–2024)",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Sen’s slope = %.4f m⁴/s⁴/month (%.2f m⁴/s⁴/decade, %.1f%% change since 1958–1967)\nPre-whitened MK p = %.4f",
      slope_monthly_svalbard, slope_decade_svalbard, pct_change_svalbard, mk_pw_svalbard$p.value
    ),
    x = "Date (month-end)",
    y = expression("Storminess index [m"^4*"/s"^4*"]")
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "10 years",
    date_labels = "%b-%Y",
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
  )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Final Console Summary
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================================\n")
cat("                FINAL RESULTS FOR SVALBARD REGION\n")
cat("========================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Trend Magnitude (Sen's slope): %.4f m⁴/s⁴ per decade\n", slope_decade_svalbard))
cat(sprintf("Significance (Pre-whitened MK p-value): %.4f\n", mk_pw_svalbard$p.value))
cat(sprintf("Total change (1958–2024): %.2f m⁴/s⁴ (%.1f%%)\n",
            total_change_svalbard, pct_change_svalbard))

if (mk_pw_svalbard$p.value < 0.05) {
  direction <- ifelse(sens_svalbard$estimates > 0, "INCREASING", "DECREASING")
  cat(sprintf("\nCONCLUSION: A STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT %s TREND DETECTED.\n", direction))
} else {
  cat("\nCONCLUSION: No statistically significant trend detected for the Svalbard region.\n")
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# PHASE 2.2: SPATIAL TREND ANALYSIS - FULL DOMAIN (56-90°N)
# ============================================================================
################################################################################
# Spatial trend analysis with robust pre-whitening + FDR + Monte-Carlo field
# significance (block-resampling preserving spatial covariance).
#
# Inputs expected in workspace:
#   - storminess : array [time, lat, lon] (monthly storminess, truncated to 1958-2024)
#   - lat        : numeric vector (length = n_lat)
#   - lon        : numeric vector (length = n_lon)
#   - time_dates : Date vector (length = n_time) (optional)
#
# Outputs (saved when missing):
#   - E:/ERA5_data/processed/storminess_trend_slope_full_1958-2024.nc
#   - E:/ERA5_data/processed/storminess_trend_pvalue_full_1958-2024.nc
#   - E:/ERA5_data/processed/storminess_lag1autocorr_full_1958-2024.nc
#   - E:/ERA5_data/processed/storminess_trend_counts_mc.RDS   (Monte-Carlo summary)
#
# Packages required:
#   trend, ncdf4, zoo, foreach, doParallel, pbapply
#
# Author: adapted for Francesco — ready to run
################################################################################

# -------------------------
# Config / user options
# -------------------------
processed_dir <- "E:/ERA5_data/processed"
slope_path <- file.path(processed_dir, "storminess_trend_slope_full_1958-2024.nc")
pval_path  <- file.path(processed_dir, "storminess_trend_pvalue_full_1958-2024.nc")
rho1_path  <- file.path(processed_dir, "storminess_lag1autocorr_full_1958-2024.nc")
mc_summary_path <- file.path(processed_dir, "storminess_trend_counts_mc.RDS")

min_coverage_frac <- 0.80    # require at least 80% valid months to analyze a grid cell
min_length_for_mk  <- 8      # minimal length to run Mann-Kendall
min_length_for_acf <- 12     # minimal length to estimate AR(1)
fdr_alpha <- 0.05

# Monte Carlo options
do_montecarlo <- TRUE
n_mc <- 500                 # number of Monte Carlo resamples (500-1000 typical)
block_length <- 12          # block length in months (preserves seasonal-like blocks). adjust if desired
n_cores <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1)  # cores for parallel MC

# Packages (load here)
required_pkgs <- c("trend", "ncdf4", "zoo", "foreach", "doParallel", "pbapply")
missing_pkgs <- required_pkgs[!(required_pkgs %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])]
if (length(missing_pkgs)) stop("Install required packages first: ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "))

library(trend); library(ncdf4); library(zoo)
library(foreach); library(doParallel); library(pbapply)

# Create processed dir (if not exists)
if (!dir.exists(processed_dir)) dir.create(processed_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# -------------------------
# Helper: load data if not present
# -------------------------
if (!exists("storminess") || !exists("lat") || !exists("lon")) {
  cat("storminess/lat/lon not found in workspace. Attempting to load from NetCDF (storminess file)...\n")
  storm_path <- file.path(processed_dir, "ERA5_storminess_index_monthly_1958-2024.nc")
  if (!file.exists(storm_path)) stop("Cannot find storminess file: ", storm_path)
  nc <- nc_open(storm_path)
  storminess <- ncvar_get(nc, "storminess_index")
  # storminess may be [lon, lat, time] as you described earlier - detect and transpose if needed
  dims_nc <- names(nc$dim)
  nc_close(nc)
  # If storminess dim order is [lon, lat, time], transform to [time, lat, lon]
  if (length(dim(storminess)) == 3 && dim(storminess)[1] == length(lon) && dim(storminess)[2] == length(lat)) {
    # assume current order is [lon, lat, time] -> permute to [time, lat, lon]
    storminess <- aperm(storminess, c(3, 2, 1))
  }
  # If time vector available in file, user should have set time_dates; otherwise we skip time-dependent checks
}

# Validate dims
if (length(dim(storminess)) != 3) stop("storminess must be a 3D array [time, lat, lon]")
n_time <- dim(storminess)[1]; n_lat <- dim(storminess)[2]; n_lon <- dim(storminess)[3]
cat(sprintf("Data loaded: time=%d, lat=%d, lon=%d\n", n_time, n_lat, n_lon))

# -------------------------
# Skip major processing if outputs exist
# -------------------------
outputs_exist <- file.exists(slope_path) && file.exists(pval_path) && file.exists(rho1_path)
if (outputs_exist && (!do_montecarlo || file.exists(mc_summary_path))) {
  cat("All output files already exist. Skipping computation.\n")
  cat("If you want to force re-run, delete the output files and run again.\n")
  quit(save = "no")
}

# -------------------------
# Pre-alloc output grids
# -------------------------
slope_grid <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_lat, ncol = n_lon)   # lat x lon
pval_grid  <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_lat, ncol = n_lon)
rho1_grid  <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_lat, ncol = n_lon)

# -------------------------
# Main grid loop (serial, robust)
# -------------------------
cat("Starting grid-cell trend analysis (serial loop) ...\n")
start_time <- Sys.time()
cells_processed <- 0
cells_with_data <- 0

for (i in seq_len(n_lat)) {
  for (j in seq_len(n_lon)) {
    ts_cell <- storminess[, i, j]    # time, scalar
    
    # Skip fully NA cells (likely land/outside mask)
    if (all(is.na(ts_cell))) next
    
    # Require minimal coverage
    valid_frac <- sum(!is.na(ts_cell)) / length(ts_cell)
    if (valid_frac < min_coverage_frac) next
    
    # Fill small gaps (linear interp), then locf to fill ends
    if (any(is.na(ts_cell))) {
      ts_cell <- tryCatch({
        tmp <- na.approx(ts_cell, na.rm = FALSE)
        tmp <- na.locf(tmp, na.rm = FALSE)
        tmp <- na.locf(tmp, fromLast = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE)
        tmp
      }, error = function(e) NA)
      if (any(is.na(ts_cell))) next
    }
    
    cells_with_data <- cells_with_data + 1
    
    # Robust lag-1 ACF
    rho1 <- NA_real_
    if (length(ts_cell) >= min_length_for_acf && var(ts_cell, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
      acf_res <- tryCatch(acf(ts_cell, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE, na.action = na.pass), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (!is.null(acf_res) && length(acf_res$acf) >= 2) rho1 <- as.numeric(acf_res$acf[2])
    }
    rho1_grid[i, j] <- rho1
    
    # Pre-whitening if meaningful
    n <- length(ts_cell)
    if (is.na(rho1) || n < min_length_for_acf) {
      pw_ts <- ts_cell
    } else {
      pw_ts <- ts_cell[2:n] - rho1 * ts_cell[1:(n-1)]
    }
    
    # Mann-Kendall on pw series (if long enough)
    if (length(pw_ts) >= min_length_for_mk) {
      mk_res <- tryCatch(mk.test(pw_ts), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (!is.null(mk_res)) pval_grid[i, j] <- mk_res$p.value
    } else {
      pval_grid[i, j] <- NA_real_
    }
    
    # Sen's slope on original (robust magnitude), convert to per-decade
    sens <- tryCatch(sens.slope(ts_cell), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(sens) && !is.na(sens$estimates)) {
      slope_grid[i, j] <- as.numeric(sens$estimates) * 12 * 10
    } else {
      slope_grid[i, j] <- NA_real_
    }
    
    cells_processed <- cells_processed + 1
  }
  if (i %% 3 == 0) {
    elapsed <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins"))
    cat(sprintf("  Row %3d/%3d | processed-cells: %4d | rows elapsed: %.1f min\n", i, n_lat, cells_with_data, elapsed))
  }
}

end_time <- Sys.time()
cat(sprintf("Grid loop complete. Runtime: %.1f minutes\n", difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "mins")))

# -------------------------
# Summary & FDR correction
# -------------------------
# How many p-values are below nominal alpha?
valid_pvals <- !is.na(pval_grid)
n_total_pvals <- sum(valid_pvals)
n_nominal_sig <- sum(pval_grid[valid_pvals] < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("Nominal significant cells (p<0.05): %d / %d (%.2f%%)\n",
            n_nominal_sig, n_total_pvals, 100 * n_nominal_sig / n_total_pvals))

# FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg)
pvec <- as.vector(pval_grid)
valid_idx <- which(!is.na(pvec))
adj_pvec <- rep(NA_real_, length(pvec))
if (length(valid_idx) > 0) {
  adj_pvec[valid_idx] <- p.adjust(pvec[valid_idx], method = "BH")
}
adj_pval_grid <- matrix(adj_pvec, nrow = n_lat, ncol = n_lon)
n_fdr_sig <- sum(adj_pval_grid < fdr_alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("FDR-significant cells (q<%.2f): %d / %d (%.2f%%)\n",
            fdr_alpha, n_fdr_sig, n_total_pvals, 100 * n_fdr_sig / n_total_pvals))

# -------------------------
# Monte Carlo field-significance via block resampling (preserves spatial covariance)
# -------------------------
mc_results <- list()
if (do_montecarlo) {
  cat("Starting Monte Carlo field-significance test (block-resampling)...\n")
  cat(sprintf(" n_mc = %d, block_length = %d months, n_cores = %d\n", n_mc, block_length, n_cores))
  
  # Observed count to compare to MC:
  observed_count <- n_nominal_sig
  
  # Build list of block start indices (non-overlapping block positions)
  # We'll create surrogate time series by sampling blocks with replacement,
  # using the same block sequence for every grid cell (keeps spatial covariance).
  n_blocks <- ceiling(n_time / block_length)
  block_starts <- seq(1, n_time, by = block_length)
  
  # Create vector of block indices (start positions) used to slice original times
  all_block_idx <- lapply(block_starts, function(s) {
    end_idx <- min(n_time, s + block_length - 1)
    seq(s, end_idx)
  })
  # To allow uniform sampling, ensure each block has exactly block_length by wrapping (circular)
  block_series <- lapply(block_starts, function(s) {
    idx <- seq(s, s + block_length - 1)
    ((idx - 1) %% n_time) + 1
  })
  
  # Parallel cluster for MC
  cl <- makeCluster(min(n_cores, parallel::detectCores()))
  registerDoParallel(cl)
  on.exit({
    stopCluster(cl)
    registerDoSEQ()
  }, add = TRUE)
  
  # Function to build surrogate by sampling blocks (same block sequence applied to all grid cells)
  build_surrogate_indices <- function() {
    chosen_blocks <- sample(seq_along(block_series), size = n_blocks, replace = TRUE)
    idx_concat <- unlist(block_series[chosen_blocks])
    # keep first n_time elements
    idx_concat[1:n_time]
  }
  
  # MC loop (parallel)
  mc_counts <- foreach(iter = seq_len(n_mc), .packages = c("trend", "zoo"), .combine = c) %dopar% {
    # build time index for surrogate
    idx_surr <- build_surrogate_indices()
    
    # Build surrogate field by reindexing time dimension
    # This reorders the time slices identically for all grid cells (preserves spatial covariance)
    surr_field <- storminess[idx_surr, , , drop = FALSE]
    
    # For performance, compute trends only for valid cells (same mask from original)
    # We'll reproduce the same analysis: gap-fill small holes using same routine,
    # then compute MK on pre-whitened series (if length >= min) and Sen's slope for magnitude,
    # and count how many have p < 0.05.
    surr_pvals <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_lat, ncol = n_lon)
    
    for (ii in seq_len(n_lat)) {
      for (jj in seq_len(n_lon)) {
        ts_s <- surr_field[, ii, jj]
        if (all(is.na(ts_s))) next
        valid_frac_s <- sum(!is.na(ts_s)) / length(ts_s)
        if (valid_frac_s < min_coverage_frac) next
        if (any(is.na(ts_s))) {
          ts_s <- tryCatch({
            tmp <- na.approx(ts_s, na.rm = FALSE)
            tmp <- na.locf(tmp, na.rm = FALSE)
            tmp <- na.locf(tmp, fromLast = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE)
            tmp
          }, error = function(e) NA)
          if (any(is.na(ts_s))) next
        }
        # acf/rho1
        rho1_s <- NA_real_
        if (length(ts_s) >= min_length_for_acf && var(ts_s, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
          acf_res_s <- tryCatch(acf(ts_s, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE, na.action = na.pass), error = function(e) NULL)
          if (!is.null(acf_res_s) && length(acf_res_s$acf) >= 2) rho1_s <- as.numeric(acf_res_s$acf[2])
        }
        n_s <- length(ts_s)
        if (is.na(rho1_s) || n_s < min_length_for_acf) {
          pw_s <- ts_s
        } else {
          pw_s <- ts_s[2:n_s] - rho1_s * ts_s[1:(n_s-1)]
        }
        if (length(pw_s) >= min_length_for_mk) {
          mk_r <- tryCatch(mk.test(pw_s), error = function(e) NULL)
          if (!is.null(mk_r)) surr_pvals[ii, jj] <- mk_r$p.value
        }
      }
    }
    # count nominal p<0.05 (same as observed numerator)
    sum(surr_pvals < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
  } # end foreach
  
  # collect results
  stopCluster(cl)
  registerDoSEQ()
  mc_counts <- unlist(mc_counts)
  mc_results$counts <- mc_counts
  mc_results$observed_count <- observed_count
  mc_results$alpha <- 0.05
  
  # compute MC p-value: proportion of MC iterations with count >= observed (two-sided rarely used here)
  p_mc <- mean(mc_counts >= observed_count)
  mc_results$p_value <- p_mc
  mc_results$summary <- list(mean = mean(mc_counts), sd = sd(mc_counts),
                             quantiles = quantile(mc_counts, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)))
  
  # Save MC summary to disk
  saveRDS(mc_results, mc_summary_path)
  cat(sprintf("Monte Carlo done. Observed significant cells = %d; MC p-value = %.4f\n", observed_count, p_mc))
} else {
  cat("Skipping Monte-Carlo as requested.\n")
}

# -------------------------
# Save NetCDF outputs (latitude x longitude ordering)
# -------------------------
cat("Saving NetCDF outputs (latitude x longitude ordering)...\n")

# Define dims
lat_dim <- ncdim_def("latitude", "degrees_north", lat)
lon_dim <- ncdim_def("longitude", "degrees_east", lon)

# slope variable
slope_var <- ncvar_def("trend_slope", "m4 s-4 decade-1", list(lat_dim, lon_dim), -9999.0,
                       longname = "Sen slope trend (storminess) per decade", prec = "float")
nc_slope <- nc_create(slope_path, slope_var)
ncvar_put(nc_slope, slope_var, slope_grid)
ncatt_put(nc_slope, 0, "title", "Storminess: Sen slope per decade (1958-2024)")
ncatt_put(nc_slope, 0, "created_by", Sys.info()[["user"]])
ncatt_put(nc_slope, 0, "creation_date", as.character(Sys.time()))
nc_close(nc_slope)

# pvalue var
pval_var <- ncvar_def("p_value", "1", list(lat_dim, lon_dim), -9999.0,
                      longname = "Pre-whitened Mann-Kendall p-value", prec = "float")
nc_pval <- nc_create(pval_path, pval_var)
ncvar_put(nc_pval, pval_var, pval_grid)
ncatt_put(nc_pval, 0, "note", "Nominal p-values; use FDR-adjusted results for multiple-testing conclusions")
nc_close(nc_pval)

# rho1 var
rho1_var <- ncvar_def("lag1_autocorr", "1", list(lat_dim, lon_dim), -9999.0,
                      longname = "Lag-1 autocorrelation (rho1)", prec = "float")
nc_rho1 <- nc_create(rho1_path, rho1_var)
ncvar_put(nc_rho1, rho1_var, rho1_grid)
nc_close(nc_rho1)

cat("Files saved:\n")
cat(" -", slope_path, "\n")
cat(" -", pval_path, "\n")
cat(" -", rho1_path, "\n")
if (do_montecarlo) cat(" -", mc_summary_path, "\n")

# -------------------------
# Final report summary
# -------------------------
cat("\nFinal summary:\n")
cat(sprintf("Total grid cells (lat*lon): %d\n", n_lat * n_lon))
cat(sprintf("Cells with enough data: %d\n", cells_with_data))
cat(sprintf("Nominal significant (p<0.05): %d\n", n_nominal_sig))
cat(sprintf("FDR-significant (q<%.2f): %d\n", fdr_alpha, n_fdr_sig))
if (do_montecarlo) cat(sprintf("Monte-Carlo p-value for field significance (observed count): %.4f\n", mc_results$p_value))

cat("\nDone.\n")

```

# --- Load data ---
dir_proc <- "E:/ERA5_data/processed"
f_slope <- file.path(dir_proc, "storminess_trend_slope_full_1958-2024.nc")
f_pval  <- file.path(dir_proc, "storminess_trend_pvalue_full_1958-2024.nc")

# --- Basic global stats ---

            mean(rho1, na.rm=TRUE), median(rho1, na.rm=TRUE)))

# --- Zonal (latitude-band) means ---

zonal_means <- data.frame(lat_band = levels(lat_band),

    y = "Grid-cell count"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

# --- Map of slopes with significance overlay ---

# --- Map of slopes with significance overlay ---
ggplot() +

  geom_raster(data = df, aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = slope)) +

  # Visual settings

    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1.8, xlim = c(-180, 180), ylim = c(56, 90)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  labs(
    title = "Storminess Trend (1958–2024)",
    subtitle = "Contours = locally p < 0.05 (uncorrected)",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

# --- Monte-Carlo distribution plot ---
hist(mc_res$counts, breaks=30, col="grey70",

     xlab="Number of significant cells (p < 0.05)")
abline(v = mc_res$observed_count, col="red", lwd=2)
text(mc_res$observed_count, max(hist(mc_res$counts, plot=FALSE)$counts)*0.9,
     labels = sprintf("Observed = %d\np_MC = %.3f",
                      mc_res$observed_count, mc_res$p_value),
     pos=4, col="red")

# ============================================================================
# Figure 2: Publication-Quality Polar Map
# ============================================================================
# --- 1. Load Data and Keep in Lat/Lon Format ---
# We DO NOT project the rasters. We load them and convert directly to a data frame.
cat("Loading raster data in native lat/lon...\n")
slope_rast_lonlat <- rast("E:/ERA5_data/processed/storminess_trend_slope_full_1958-2024.nc")
pval_rast_lonlat <- rast("E:/ERA5_data/processed/storminess_trend_pvalue_full_1958-2024.nc")

slope_df <- as.data.frame(slope_rast_lonlat, xy = TRUE)
names(slope_df) <- c("x", "y", "slope")
pval_df <- as.data.frame(pval_rast_lonlat, xy = TRUE)
names(pval_df) <- c("x", "y", "p_value")

plot_df <- left_join(slope_df, pval_df, by = c("x", "y")) %>%
  mutate(significant = !is.na(p_value) & p_value < 0.05) %>%
  filter(!is.na(slope))

# --- 2. Prepare Coastlines (also in Lat/Lon) ---
cat("Loading coastline data in native lat/lon...\n")
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# Repair geometry just in case, but DO NOT project yet.
world_valid <- st_make_valid(world)

# --- 3. Create the Final Polar Plot ---
cat("Generating final publication-quality polar map...\n")

polar_trend_map <- ggplot() +
  # a. Plot the trend data using the original lon/lat columns
  geom_tile(data = plot_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = slope)) +

  # b. Define the color scale
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    name = "Trend\n(m⁴/s⁴ per decade)",
    colors = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    limits = c(-max(abs(plot_df$slope)), max(abs(plot_df$slope))),
    na.value = "transparent"
  ) +

  # c. Add the lat/lon coastlines
  geom_sf(data = world_valid, fill = "grey60", color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +

  # d. Add stippling using the original lon/lat columns
  geom_point(data = filter(plot_df, significant == TRUE),
             aes(x = x, y = y),
             shape = 16, size = 0.5, color = "black") +

  # e. **THE DEFINITIVE FIX:**
  # Apply the polar projection and set the view using DEGREES.
  # This is the most robust way to crop a polar plot.
  coord_sf(
    crs = "+proj=laea +lat_0=90 +lon_0=0", # The target projection
    default_crs = st_crs(4326),          # Tells ggplot our geom_tile is lat/lon
    ylim = c(56, 90),                      # Crop the view from 56°N to the pole
    expand = FALSE
  ) +

  # f. Add labels and a clean theme
  labs(
    title = "Spatial Trend in Arctic Storminess (1958-2024)",
    subtitle = "Trend magnitude with stippling for regions of nominal significance (p < 0.05)",
    caption = "Data: ERA5 | Method: Pre-whitened Mann-Kendall & Theil-Sen Slope"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90"),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "white", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank()
  )

# --- 4. Save the Plot ---
ggsave("Arctic_Storminess_Polar_Trend_Map_FINAL.png",
       plot = polar_trend_map,
       width = 10, height = 10, units = "in", dpi = 300)

cat("✓ Final polar map saved as Arctic_Storminess_Polar_Trend_Map_FINAL.png\n")
print(polar_trend_map)
